Should Palisade raise prices while churn is rising? Discussion document for the CEO and leadership team
Palisade Docs
CEO and leadership team
Synthetic benchmark data: the company and all figures are fictional

slides.title: Key questions

paragraphs.text: Key questions
Should Palisade raise prices at its 2027 renewals while churn is rising, and if so where and by how much, to grow ARR at least 15% with NRR above 100%?
Why is churn rising, and is it a sign that customers are pushing back on price?
Will mid-market and enterprise customers accept a 2027 price rise?
What would a 2027 rise cost in SMB, now that Inkwell sells a $9 plan?
Which option delivers 15% ARR growth with NRR above 100%?
How should the rise roll out, and what tells us to stop?
Decision maker
Success criteria
Timing
Out of scope
CEO and leadership team, approving the 2027 pricing plan
ARR grows at least 15% in 2027, from $86.0M; Net revenue retention stays above 100% overall; Price changes respect renewal dates and enterprise contract terms
Leadership pricing decision, December 2026
New plans or packaging; Usage-based pricing; Renegotiating enterprise caps; 2027 acquisition plan

slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Raise prices on mid-market and enterprise renewals in 2027; hold SMB prices until a test shows a rise is safe
Rising churn comes from the 2025 promotion cohort, not from a reaction to list prices
–	About 90% of the rise in lost customers is promotion customers
–	Fixing the promotion cohort cuts SMB churn by a third, not by half
Larger customers should carry a 10% rise, checked against a renewal control group
–	A 10% rise left mid-market conversion at 23.1% against 23.6%
SMB is where a rise could backfire: Inkwell sells at $9 against our $15
–	Win rate in SMB deals with Inkwell fell from 51% to 38% in a year
–	A 12% rise stops paying at twice the 2023 churn response
A segmented rise adds about $4.3M and can reach 15% growth with little new business
–	The CFO's $10.3M is about $6.3M after timing, caps and churn
–	Only $0.6M of new ARR is needed; NRR rises to about 114%
Reprice larger renewals in January, test SMB first, and re-activate the cohort
–	Decide SMB prices in July against the 2023 response
